properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 9 at 4:59AM CDT until September 12 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

Raccoon River at Des Moines Fleur Dr affecting Polk County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Raccoon River at Des Moines Fleur Dr, or from Walnut Creek
to the Des Moines River.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.3 feet, SW 30th St is closed from George Flagg
Parkway to Bell Ave. George Flagg Parkway is closed from SW 30th St
to SW 28th St.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:47 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 11.2 feet, and rising.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 13.1 feet early Friday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

River forecasts include observed precipitation plus forecast
precipitation over the next 24 hours.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 8 at 10:05PM CDT until September 9 at 8:20PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday was 26.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 18.8 feet Sunday
evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.2
feet on 03/19/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL WEDNESDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 9 at 1:49AM CDT until September 9 at 7:45AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
FFWDMX

The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Dallas County in central Iowa...
Southern Polk County in central Iowa...
Northern Madison County in south central Iowa...
Northern Warren County in south central Iowa...
Northern Adair County in southwestern Iowa...
Northern Cass County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Audubon County in west central Iowa...
Southern Guthrie County in west central Iowa...

* Until 745 AM CDT.

* At 149 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4.5 inches of rain
have fallen, with locally higher amounts. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area through
sunrise. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Des Moines, West Des Moines, Ankeny, Urbandale, Johnston, Clive,
Indianola, Altoona, Waukee, Norwalk, Pleasant Hill, Grimes,
Atlantic, Adel, Guthrie Center, Windsor Heights, Carlisle,
Bondurant, Saylorville and Mitchellville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 9 at 2:30AM CDT until September 9 at 7:30AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
FFWOAX

The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Harrison County in southwestern Iowa...
Northwestern Mills County in southwestern Iowa...
Pottawattamie County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Shelby County in southwestern Iowa...
Southeastern Dodge County in east central Nebraska...
Douglas County in east central Nebraska...
Sarpy County in east central Nebraska...
Eastern Saunders County in east central Nebraska...
Southeastern Washington County in east central Nebraska...

* Until 730 AM CDT.

* At 230 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. This heavy rain could
especially affect portions of north Omaha as storms train
over the area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Omaha, Council Bluffs, Bellevue, Papillion, Blair, Ralston, Wahoo,
Gretna, Bennington, Boys Town, Elkhorn, Offutt AFB, Millard, La
Vista, Carter Lake, Missouri Valley, Valley, Oakland and Avoca.
